newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo dinar recovers some losses on black market.
newsitem.headline: Yugo dinar recovers some losses on black market.

text.p: Yugoslavia's dinar recovered some of its losses on the black market on Wednesday to trade at 4.2 to the German mark, street dealers said.
The dinar changed hands at 4.3 to the mark on Tuesday.

Traders on the official Belgrade bourse told Reuters the dinar's New Year and Christmas slide was provoked by a substantial increase in money supply in the last days of 1996. Before the holidays, the dinar stood at 3.8 to the mark.

"The bourse, itself, sees no improvement in the liquidity of the banking sector. Banks' balances remain in the red and along with their insolvency, we witness an obvious expansion in money supply going directly onto the streets," a trader said.
The opposition, which has staged seven weeks of protests against President Slobodna Milosevic, accuses the government of printing money to pay wage arrears owed to the police.
Traders said the dinar's fall ended its year-long stability, which had been one of the few factors the government could depend on.

Yugoslavia's government vowed to keep the dinar stable and fixed at 3.3 to the mark in 1997, but traders viewed the latest developments as the government's attempt to protect itself and save social peace at expense of economic stability. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
